stories.title: 'Straw bombs' helping to prevent flooding in Pine Valley

With 130 helicopter trips in a single day, this innovative approach is already showing results: recent flood reports are good, and the community remains safe.

stories.title: At San Francisco General, Researchers Are Learning How To Control HIV Without Drugs
stories.summary: After three decades treating HIV patients at San Francisco General, Dr. Steven Deeks and his team have evidence the immune system itself can be trained to control HIV — without drugs. Ten patients each made about 50 visits in an intensive study that could change what long-term treatment looks like.
stories.extended_summary: Stop the drugs, and HIV almost always comes back. That's been the rule for decades — until now. At San Francisco General's legendary Ward 86, Dr. Steven Deeks has spent 30-plus years asking why some patients' immune systems fight HIV better than others. Starting in 2020, ten people with HIV each made roughly 50 visits for an intensive study testing experimental treatments designed to strengthen different parts of the immune response. Then, under close supervision, they paused their medication. The results offer the first real evidence that the immune system can be trained to keep HIV in check on its own — a potential seismic shift in a field where 40 million lives have been lost.
